title: February Reading Corner: Understanding Decoding Skills
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TITLE 

TALK 

READING 

CORNER

TITLE TALK READING CORNER

February Newsletter
What does decoding mean?A simple definition for decoding is recognizing letter sounds or patterns and blending them together to translate a written word into speech. Decoding is a foundational reading skill (phonics) that must be developed to begin successful reading with fluency. This process begins with students recognizing their letters and sounds then blending the sounds to speak the word, i.e., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes cat.Here is an example of what happens when a student decodes a word:Recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh)Knowing the sounds they makeBlending those sounds together to read a wordActivities: Reading Rockets is a reputable research-based website for all things reading; and below are age-specific resources for decoding activities.Kindergarten:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101Kindergartener phonics and decoding activitiesFirst Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesSecond Grade:https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activitiesThird Grade:Here is a video showing how a 3rd grade student uses syllables to decode longer words more easily.

summary: **Decoding** is the foundational reading skill of recognizing letter sounds and patterns and blending them together to read words aloud. The process involves recognizing letters and letter patterns (like b, sh, igh), knowing their sounds, and blending those sounds to read words (e.g., /c/ - /a/ - /t/ becomes "cat"). Grade-specific decoding activities and resources are available from Reading Rockets for [Kindergarten](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101), [First Grade](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-first-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities), [Second Grade](https://www.readingrockets.org/literacy-home/reading-101-guide-parents/your-second-grader/phonics-and-decoding-activities), and Third Grade (video showing syllable strategies for longer words).

&

NEWS & INFORMATION

As we wrap up another great week of learning, we are keeping a close eye on the upcoming cold weather. Please be sure your child comes to school dressed warmly each day, including coats, hats, and gloves. With the possibility of weather-related delays or closures, it is extremely important that your phone numbers and email addresses are up to date in our system so we can reach you quickly with important information.  If your family is in need of a warm place during extreme temperatures, local warming centers are available throughout the community, please see below for that information. Thank you for partnering with us to keep our students safe, warm, and supported—your continued communication and support make a big difference!Sincerely,Mrs. Jones, Principal

summary: Students should dress warmly with coats, hats, and gloves for the upcoming cold weather. Families must ensure their contact information is current in the school system to receive timely notifications about possible weather delays or closures. **Local warming centers** are available throughout the community during extreme temperatures January 23-27, 2026, including multiple library locations and the City of Monroe Police Department (open 24 hours). For more information on warming center hours and locations, visit https://www.bcohio.gov or https://www.midpointelibrary.org/.

title: Reading Corner January Newsletter on Fluency
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
TITLE 

TALK 

CORNER

TITLE TALK CORNER

summary:
The January Reading Corner newsletter focuses on **reading fluency** - the ability to read accurately, at an appropriate pace, and with expression. Fluency develops through regular reading and rereading of books and passages, not just memorizing sight words. **Simple ways families can support fluency include:**
- Read and reread familiar books, stories, or short passages
- Practice sight words as part of reading, not just in isolation
- Read aloud to model smooth, expressive reading
- Talk briefly about the story to support understanding

**Helpful resource:** Reading Rockets offers family-friendly tips and videos for supporting fluent reading at home. Contact your student's Reading Corner Teacher for help with these activities.

source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:

NURSE'S CORNER

summary: The school is experiencing an increase in flu and seasonal illnesses. **Keep your child home if they have:** fever (100°F or higher), vomiting or diarrhea, significant cough, sore throat with fever, body aches, extreme fatigue, or flu-like symptoms. Students must be **fever-free for 24 hours without medication** and **symptom-free for 24 hours after vomiting or diarrhea** before returning to school.
